name: Strait-spanning nanotube bridge
subtitle: suspension bridges that cross ten-kilometre straits

effects.effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal

effect: rolled-up carbon sheets are stronger than steel and conduct like metal
how: Suspension bridges top out at about two kilometres because longer steel cables get too heavy to hold up even themselves, so straits like Gibraltar have no crossing. Cables of nanotube fibre, many times stronger than steel for their weight, could hold spans several times longer and link continents by road and rail.
obstacle: Nobody can yet make nanotube cable by the thousands of tonnes, and how it stretches under decades of load is unknown.
why: The longest span is two kilometres of steel; nanotube cable exists only in short lengths.
real: Carpinteri & Pugno (2008) and an MIT thesis model nanotube-cable super-bridges with spans of 5+ km, but no nanotube bridge cable has been built.
